title: Clashes Intensify at Point Zéro in Mwenga, Opening New Front as Fighting Spreads Into Fizi Highlands
detail: Armed clashes intensified from the morning of Sept 19, 2026 at Point Zéro in Mwenga territory, South Kivu, pitting a FARDC-Wazalendo coalition backed by Burundian forces (FDNB) against an AFC/Red Tabara-Twirwaneho coalition. Fighting spread into neighboring Fizi territory, reaching the villages of Natulonge, Kabindo, Biziba and Irumba, according to local sources and civil society structures. The violence forced civilians to flee their homes and disrupted agricultural and commercial activity across the highlands and plateaus of Fizi, Uvira and Itombwe — a new front opening even as government forces consolidated gains in the Masisi-Walikale-Kalehe corridor further north. No casualty toll was available and none of the armed actors issued a public statement.

title: Ebola Toll Reaches 3,639 Deaths Among 7,541 Cases as Outbreak Spreads to Seventh Province, Sud-Ubangi
detail: DRC's National Institute of Public Health (INSP) reported 7,541 confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) cases and 3,639 deaths as of Sept 18 data, a 48.3% case-fatality rate, with 1,823 people recovered. The outbreak now spans 62 health zones across seven provinces after Sud-Ubangi was newly affected by an imported case confirmed Sept 10 — an area of roughly 240,000 square kilometers, comparable to the United Kingdom. Officials said the national case curve has reached a "plateau" after rapid growth, but cautioned that "no one can say the epidemic is under control." In Ituri, the epicenter where transmission is beginning to slow, roughly 300 new cases and 160 deaths were still recorded in the preceding week alone.

media.caption: DRC's Ebola outbreak response as the toll reached 7,541 cases and 3,639 deaths across seven provinces, Sept 18-19, 2026

confidenceReason: Figures are attributed directly to DRC's INSP national tally and corroborated by both RT en français and UN News/ONU Info reporting on the same data.

title: Ervebo Vaccine Clinical Trial Launches in Bunia to Test Efficacy Against Bundibugyo Strain
detail: Healthcare workers in Bunia, Ituri province, received the first doses Saturday, Sept 19, 2026 as part of a clinical trial of the Ervebo vaccine targeting 20,000 people over 9-12 months. Ervebo is already proven effective against the Zaire ebolavirus strain; the trial aims to establish whether it also protects against the Bundibugyo strain driving the current outbreak, for which no specific vaccine or treatment yet exists. The initiative had already vaccinated more than 3,000 people in Tshopo province and over 700 in Bas-Uélé. DRC's national Ebola response is directed by Prof. Steve Ahuka, with Médecins Sans Frontières participating through researcher Dr. Nana Mimbu. The outbreak is DRC's 17th Ebola epidemic and its deadliest on record.

media.caption: A clinical trial of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine launched for healthcare workers in Bunia, Ituri, Sept 19, 2026

title: Joint PNC-FARDC Sweep in Beni's Malepe Neighborhood Nets 28 Arrests, Including Two Soldiers
detail: The Congolese National Police (PNC) and FARDC jointly conducted an early-morning security sweep of Beni's Malepe neighborhood on Sept 19, 2026, under orders from the provincial police commissioner and the urban police commander. Twenty-eight people were apprehended, including two FARDC soldiers and seven women, and authorities seized two firearms and more than 169 cartridges. The operation targeted rising urban criminality following the Sept 9-16 triple killing of a money changer, his wife and a moto-taxi driver in Beni's Butanuka neighborhood, and was aimed partly at questioning the detained soldiers to trace the source of illicit weapons.
